courses.title: Intermediate Architectural Design 1
courses.description: The design process as it relates to building materials and construction and the interaction of aesthetic, technological and economic determinants. Introduction to building codes. Corequisite(s): ARC 5031A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; ARC 502 or ARC 5020; and ARC 502L, ARC 5021L, or ARC 5021A and ARC 5021.

courses.title: Intermediate Architectural Design 1 Activity
courses.description: The design process as it relates to building materials and construction and the interaction of aesthetic, technological and economic determinants. Introduction to building codes. All prerequisites must be successfully completed with a letter grade of a C or higher to qualify for enrollment in this course. Corequisite(s): ARC 5031 , ARC 5521A , ARC 5520A , and ARC 5522A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; ARC 502 or ARC 5020 ; ARC 502L, ARC 5021L , OR ARC 5021A and ARC 5021 ; ARC 5210 ; and ARC 5212 .

courses.title: Intermediate Architectural Design 2
courses.description: Interaction of construction technology, human behavior, site development in the design of multi-family housing in a specific context. Introduction to large-scale urban issues. Corequisite(s): ARC 6400 and ARC 5041A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; ARC 504 or ARC 5030; and ARC 503L, ARC 5031L, or ARC 5031A and ARC 5031.

courses.title: Intermediate Architectural Design 2 Activity
courses.description: Interaction of construction technology, human behavior, site development in the design of multi-family housing in a specific context. Introduction to large-scale urban issues. Corequisite(s): ARC 6400 and ARC 5041 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; ARC 504 or ARC 5030 ; and ARC 503L, ARC 5031L, or 5031A and ARC 5031.

courses.title: Structures 2
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 3220 The relationship of structure to form, function, and economics. Analysis of structural systems, including designing structural members in wood, steel, concrete and masonry. Corequisite(s): ARC 5222 , ARC 5031A , ARC 5031
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, ARC 5210 , and ARC 5212 ; or consent of Graduate Coordinator.

courses.title: Structures 2 Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 3222 The relationship of structure to form, function, and economics. Analysis of structural systems, including designing structural members in wood, steel, concrete and masonry. Corequisite(s): ARC 5220 , ARC 5031 , and ARC 5031A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, ARC 5210 , and ARC 5212 ; or consent of Graduate Coordinator.

courses.title: Environmental Controls 2
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 3320 . Performance principles and systems to safeguard occupant comfort while reducing environmental impact and approaching carbon neutrality. Survey of lighting, HVAC systems, acoustics, plumbing, electric and other building control systems. Corequisite(s): ARC 5322 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, ARC 5310 , and ARC 5312 ; or permission of the Graduate Coordinator.

courses.title: Environmental Controls 2 Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 3322 Performance principles and systems to safeguard occupant comfort while reducing environmental impact and approaching carbon neutrality. Survey of lighting, HVAC systems, acoustics, plumbing, electric and other building control systems. Corequisite(s): ARC 5320 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, ARC 5310 , and ARC 5312 ; or permission of the Graduate Coordinator.

courses.title: Building Construction 2
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 3420 Techniques of construction, building components, and systems investigated through case studies. Further exploration of properties of materials used in construction and their specification both in written and drawing formats. Emphasis on systems design for structure, weatherproofing and sustainable design with respect to materials selection/interaction. Corequisite(s): ARC 5452 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, ARC 5440 , and ARC 5442 ; or permission of the Graduate Coordinator.

courses.title: Building Construction 2 Discussion
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 3422 Techniques of construction, building components, and systems investigated through case studies. Further exploration of properties of materials used in construction and their specification both in written and drawing formats. Emphasis on systems design for structure, weatherproofing and sustainable design with respect to materials selection/interaction. Corequisite(s): ARC 5450 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, ARC 5440 , and ARC 5442 ; or permission of the Graduate Coordinator.

courses.title: Digital Design Tools 3 Activity
courses.description: Development of design modeling skills and techniques, with information based digital modeling. Continuation of ARC 5510 design modeling methods and techniques; introduction to moving information between multiple BIM//CAD software environments.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; and ARC 551, ARC 5510A, or ARC 5512A.

courses.title: Digital Design Tools 4 Activity
courses.description: Development of design modeling skills and techniques, with information based digital modeling. Continuation of ARC 5510A design modeling methods and techniques; introduction to moving information between multiple BIM//CAD software environments.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; ARC 551, ARC 5510A , or ARC 5521A

courses.title: Interpreting Architecture
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 4630 Interprets architecture as a physical embodiment of civilization. Discusses architecture in the context of parallel developments in art, philosophy, literature, science, and technology. Analyzes various cultural, social, and economic factors that shape the built environment.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Advanced Architectural Design 1
courses.description: Interaction of design methods, user needs, and site constraints explored in a design project. *A special section of ARC 5990L will be assigned to students who do not pass the portfolio review. Passing this class with a C or better will satisfy the portfolio requirement. Corequisite(s): ARC 6011A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; 3.0 GPA or higher; 2nd year Portfolio Review passed*; ARC 506 or ARC 5040 ; and ARC 506L, ARC 5041L, or ARC 5041A and ARC 5041 .

courses.title: Advanced Architectural Design 1 Activity
courses.description: Interaction of design methods, user needs, and site constraints explored in a design project. *A special section of ARC 5990L will be assigned to students who do not pass the portfolio review. Passing this class with a C or better will satisfy the portfolio requirement. Corequisite(s): ARC 6011 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; 3.0 GPA or higher; 2nd year Portfolio Review passed*; ARC 506 or ARC 5040 ; and ARC 506L, ARC 5041L, or ARC 5041A and ARC 5041.

courses.title: Design Development
courses.description: An overview of construction, building components, and systems investigated through case studies. Study of the connection between material properties, fabrication techniques, and building design. Corequisite(s): ARC 5041L .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing; ARC 505 or ARC 5030 .

courses.title: Advanced Digital Design Activity
courses.description: Facilitates student access to digital design drawing and modeling, tools, skills and concepts actively used in design studio. Assignments support design studio discussion with an emphasis on advanced Building Information Modeling (BIM).
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Architectural Professional Practice 1
courses.description: The administrative, legal, ethical aspects of the architectural profession and the relationship between the profession and the construction industry. Corequisite(s): ARC 6712 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing; ARC 505 and ARC 505L, or ARC 5040 and ARC 5041L .

courses.title: Architectural Professional Practice 1 Discussion
courses.description: The administrative, legal, ethical aspects of the architectural profession and the relationship between the profession and the construction industry. Discussion. Corequisite(s): ARC 6710 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing. ARC 505 and ARC 505L, or ARC 5040 and ARC 5041L .

courses.title: Architectural Professional Practice 2
courses.description: The potential roles of the architect in the development process are discussed. Issues include goals, appraisal of needs, economics, and market analysis feasibility studies, appraisal procedures, cash flow methods, financing options, decisions, design and delivery processes, involvement at levels of design decisions and project administration. Corequisite(s): ARC 6732 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing; ARC 505 and ARC 505L, or ARC 5040 and ARC 5041L .

courses.title: Architectural Professional Practice 2 Discussion
courses.description: The potential roles of the architect in the development process are discussed. Issues include goals, appraisal of needs, economics, and market analysis feasibility studies, appraisal procedures, cash flow methods, financing options, decisions, design and delivery processes, involvement at levels of design decisions and project administration. Discussion. Corequisite(s): ARC 6730 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing; ARC 505 and ARC 505L, or ARC 5040 and ARC 5041L .

courses.title: Master’s Design Project Research
courses.description: Research and programming in support of faculty-approved student’s master’s design project.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, a 3.0 GPA or higher, ARC 5041 , ARC 5041A , and ARC 6400 .

courses.title: Drawing as Theory
courses.description: Exploration of the theory and history of architectural representation. Corequisite(s): ARC 4162A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, junior standing, or senior standing.

courses.title: Drawing as Theory Activity
courses.description: Introduction to the theory and history of architectural representation through hands-on drawing instruction and expanded discussion of assigned readings. Corequisite(s): ARC 4160 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, junior standing, or senior standing.

courses.title: Advanced Urban Design
courses.description: Design research and case-study analysis of urban theories, patterns, and form. Short design project.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing, Junior Standing, or Senior Standing.

courses.title: Architecture and Urbanism
courses.description: Examination of urban theories that form the basis for the design of buildings in modern urban and suburban settings.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, junior standing, or senior standing.

courses.title: Urbanism and Film
courses.description: Survey of Los Angeles’ portrayal in film and how portrayal has affected the view of the city’s neighborhoods, their people and landscapes. Discussions on growth, infrastructure, transportation, demography, and history in relation to issues of race, class, violence, youth, fame and fortune.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing, Junior Standing, or Senior Standing.

courses.title: Advanced Structural Design
courses.description: Topics of importance centered on structural design. Emphasis is on the exploration of space, structure and performance. Utilization of geometrically complex configurations to analyze the relationship between architectural and structural design.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing, Junior Standing, or Senior Standing; ARC 4250 or Instructor Permission.

courses.title: Sustainable Technology
courses.description: Integration and management of buildings systems to minimize environmental impact and reduce a building’s environmental footprint. Topics include sustainable materials, green building design criteria, passive heating and cooling systems, active solar systems, sustainable building and energy technologies, green building rating systems. Seminar-discussion course with emphasis on student research.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3310 ; and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Tools for Sustainability
courses.description: Environmental assessment tools for sustainable design. Computational tools for the early stages of design to evaluate and estimate building performance.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3310 ; and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Advanced Architectural Lighting
courses.description: Performance analysis and design application using computer simulation and laboratory testing of luminous environment in architecture to achieve visual comfort and special lighting effects.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3310 ; and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Carbon Neutral Architectural Design
courses.description: Concepts, strategies and tools for the design of low carbon, resilient buildings. Emphasis is on design factors that affect building impact on climate. Special emphasis is on emissions embodied in materials and energy use. Implementation and development of tools and strategies to design resilient, low carbon buildings that will help to reduce anthropogenic emissions.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3310 ; and ARC 3312 .

courses.title: Advanced Architectural Materials Research
courses.description: Advanced research connecting material properties, fabrication techniques, and building design.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3420 ; and ARC 3422 .

courses.title: Digitally Enhanced Construction and Fabrication Activity
courses.description: Survey and in-depth case studies of how to manufacture, produce and build non-standard current architectural projects. Class discussions centered on issues related to traditional versus contemporary building and documentation methods. Emphasis on advanced CAD/BIM modeling and direct output to manufacturers.Hybrid Asynchronous course.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; and ARC 2501A , ARC 3420 , or ARC 5510A .

courses.title: Senior Project Research and Programming
courses.description: Site selection and analysis, and the development of a building program in support of a student’s senior project. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing, junior or senior standing, ARC 4021A , ARC 4021 , and ARC 4502A .

courses.title: Senior Project Material and Structural Integration
courses.description: Integrating senior project design with structural and nonstructural systems, materials and codes. Perform structural, code and material analyses for their individual senior project designs based on their developed designs and information from ARC 4610. Corequisite(s): ARC 4611A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC undergraduate standing and ARC 4610.

courses.title: California Architecture
courses.description: Evolution of California’s built environment comprised of designed landscapes, architecture and infrastructure. Architectural developments in response to climate, landscape and the vision of design professionals. Ongoing contribution of California design to the present. Field trips.
courses.prerequisites: ARC senior or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: Managing a Design Firm
courses.description: The study of the relationship between the architect, employee, client, and contractor; including a study of new business development strategies, winning a commission, marketing, and client communications.
courses.prerequisites: ARC 4710 and ARC 4712 or Instructor Permission.

courses.title: Teaching Practicum
courses.description: Aids instructor in preparing course material, giving software and model-making tutorials to students, facilitating in-class discussions, and engaging in student mentoring.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: Archives Practicum Activity
courses.description: Introduction to standard archival practices, focus on the specific issues associated with the arrangement and storage of architectural records and investigate projects that incorporate archival materials. Work supports activities of the ENV Archives-Special Collections.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing, Advanced Standing, or Instructor Permission.

courses.title: Indigenous Architecture
courses.description: Survey and in-depth case studies of architectural forms produced by non literate and traditional societies around the world. Emphasis given to social, cultural and cosmological factors contributing to the variety of built forms, responses of form to climate and natural conditions, materials and methods of construction, and aesthetic expression.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: Topics in Preservation
courses.description: Discussion and research in specific areas of historic preservation including the history and documentation of historical resources, resources associated with under-represented groups and emerging research into the assessment of cultural resources. Includes a design exercise involving the documentation or adaptation of a historic building.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate, senior, or junior standing; ARC 3620 ; and ARC 3622 .

courses.title: Community Practicum Service Learning
courses.description: Community-Based Design Seminar in which students will engage applied research, analysis and design demonstrated by field studies and executed design recommendations and/or project implementation.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, senior standing, junior standing, or consent of instructor; and ARC 3021A .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to three times for a total credit of 9 units.

courses.title: Design Issues in Housing
courses.description: Behavioral, social and cultural issues in housing design as they relate to domestic organization, life cycle, class and ethnicity. Considerations of function and meaning in form-making, design adaptations in light of change, and evaluation procedures.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing or Advanced Standing; and Instructor Permission.

courses.title: Healthcare Architecture, Planning and Design
courses.description: Investigation of integrated planning, design, and construction process for healthcare architecture. New paradigm shift in healthcare policies and their social and economic impacts on innovative design of healing environments. Seminar engages students in research and analysis of healthcare design topics.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing, senior standing, junior standing, or consent of instructor; and ARC 3021A .

courses.title: Integrating/Managing New Technology in Architecture Practice
courses.description: The study of the integrating expanding digital technologies for project management, billing, cost modeling, Building Information Modeling (BIM).
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Design Thinking for Managers
courses.description: Design Thinking is an iterative process in which we seek to understand the user, challenge assumptions, and redefine problems in an attempt to identify alternative strategies and solutions that might not be instantly apparent with our initial level of understanding. At the same time, Design Thinking provides a solution-based approach to solving problems. It is a way of thinking and working as well as a collection of hands-on methods.* This course will introduce students to Design Thinking through case study organizations that have adopted design thinking in their management and business practices. Design Thinking is an iterative process in which we seek to understand the user, challenge assumptions, and redefine problems in an attempt to identify alternative strategies and solutions that might not be instantly apparent with our initial level of understanding. At the same time, Design Thinking provides a solution-based approach to solving problems. It is a way of thinking and working as well as a collection of hands-on methods.* * Foundation for Interaction Design, https://www.interaction-design.org/
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Architecture Project Management
courses.description: The detailed study of the Architects role in the process of managing an Architectural Project from conception through construction and to occupancy.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Managing a Design Firm
courses.description: The study of the relationship between the architect, employee, client, and contractor; including a study of new business development strategies, winning a commission, marketing, and client communications.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Comprehensive Development Process
courses.description: The study of the role of the Architect in a comprehensive development process as a means for expanding the Architects influence over design and project outcomes.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: The Integrated Design Practice and Architecture
courses.description: The study of the changing nature of the Architectural practice and project delivery methods to include, planning, development, investment/finance, architecture, landscape, engineering, construction, interiors, real-estate sales, management professional services and Integrated Project Delivery (IPD) and design-build methods.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming and Behavioral Factors
courses.requirement: Students admitted in Advanced Standing are not required to complete these 30 units.
courses.description: Study of the role that architectural programming and behavioral factors play in the design of buildings. Architect’s responsibility to respond to the physical and social conditions of an urban context. Corequisite(s): ARC 5011A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Introduction to Architectural Design 1
courses.requirement: Students admitted in Advanced Standing are not required to complete these 30 units.
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental elements of architectural design. Corequisite(s): ARC 5011A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Introduction to Architectural Design 1 Activity
courses.requirement: Students admitted in Advanced Standing are not required to complete these 30 units.
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental elements of architectural design explored in the abstract. Emphasis on basic design, graphic communication skills and model-making. Corequisite(s): ARC 5011 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Introduction to Architectural Design 2
courses.requirement: Students admitted in Advanced Standing are not required to complete these 30 units.
courses.description: A continuation of research on simple buildings and their relationship to site and program. Introduction to architectural programming and the influence of context. Corequisite(s): ARC 5021A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; ARC 501 or ARC 5010; and ARC 501L, ARC 5011L, or ARC 5011A and ARC 5011.

courses.title: Introduction to Architectural Design 2 Activity
courses.requirement: Students admitted in Advanced Standing are not required to complete these 30 units.
courses.description: A continuation of basic design exercises focusing on simple buildings and their relationship to site and program. Introduction to architectural programming and the influence of context. Corequisite(s): ARC 5021 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing; ARC 501 or ARC 5010; and ARC 501L, ARC 5011L, or ARC 5011A and ARC 5011.

Introduction to architectural construction drawing documentation. Corequisite(s): ARC 5440 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.description: Analytical and conceptual thinking skills, and graphic and form communication skills, through the use of electronic media. State-of-the-art, raster and vector based digital schematic design tools as a foundation for information based digital design tool suites.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing and ARC 5511A .

courses.title: World Architecture from Renaissance through Modern Era
courses.requirement: Students admitted in Advanced Standing are not required to complete these 30 units.
courses.description: Cultural, social and aesthetic forces that shaped architecture and urban design during the Renaissance and Baroque periods, and from the Eighteenth, through Twentieth Centuries. Particular attention to the emergence of the Modern movement.
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: American Architecture
courses.requirement: Students admitted in Advanced Standing are not required to complete these 30 units.
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 4640 Development of American buildings and infrastructure in response to changes in material and methods of construction, demography and cultural values contributing to evolving built environment. Includes history of American architectural profession. Corequisite(s): ARC 5642 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: American Architecture Discussion
courses.requirement: Students admitted in Advanced Standing are not required to complete these 30 units.
courses.description: Dual Listed as: ARC 4642 Development of American buildings and infrastructure in response to changes in material and methods of construction, demography and cultural values contributing to evolving built environment. Includes history of American architectural profession. Corequisite(s): ARC 5640 .
courses.prerequisites: ARC graduate standing.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Material and Structures Integration
courses.description: Facilitate student mastery of the Building Systems, Construction Materials, and Structural System to be utilized in their faculty-approved master’s degree architectural design project. Corequisite(s): ARC 6951A .
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing; 3.0 GPA or higher; and ARC 691 and ARC 694, or ARC 6940 .

courses.title: Master’s Degree Project Activity
courses.description: Development of master’s degree project. Corequisite(s): ARC 6951 .
courses.prerequisites: Permission of Graduate Coordinator; ARC 6940 , or ARC 691 and ARC 694; and GPA of 3.0 or higher.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.description: Development of master’s degree thesis project.
courses.prerequisites: ARC Graduate Standing; 3.0 GPA or Higher. ARC 691 and ARC 694, or ARC 6940 .

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Graduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
